info.title: Student Voice Portal API
info.description:
Contract-first API specification for the Student Voice Portal.

All paths in this document are relative to `/api/v1`. FastAPI is the officially
selected backend framework for this project.

**Security model**
- Administrators authenticate with `POST /auth/login`. The returned JWT is
  valid for 8 hours (28,800 seconds). Every `/admin/*` operation requires that
  JWT. Missing or expired tokens return 401; inactive administrators return 403.
- The login endpoint is limited to 5 attempts per 15-minute window under US-31.
  A rate-limited request returns 429.
- Students do not have accounts. They use a tracking reference to view a
  complaint. Meeting confirmation and rescheduling require the reference in
  `X-Tracking-Reference`, and the server must verify that it belongs to the
  complaint associated with the meeting.
- Tracking and meeting-response operations must also be rate-limited before
  public deployment. Their exact thresholds are deployment/security settings
  and must be selected and tested by the team; 429 is part of their contract.
- Anonymous complaints must not store student identity or free-text
  descriptions. Student tracking responses never include student identity.

**Tracking-reference security**
The current user-story format is `SVP-` plus six uppercase alphanumeric
characters. This is approximately 31 bits of entropy and is a constrained
capability secret, not a password. Preserve the format for compatibility with
US-12, but generate it with a cryptographically secure random-number generator
(CSPRNG), retry on uniqueness collisions, rate-limit lookup/response endpoints,
and redact references from application and access logs. Before real public
exposure, the project owner should consider approving a longer reference and
update the database column, validation, UI, and API contract together.

**Shared error contract**
Every API error uses `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...",
"fields": {} } }`. Validation field values may be a string or a list of
strings. `fields` is an empty object when an error has no field-specific
details. FastAPI request/business validation failures use 422. Rate limiting
uses 429 with a `Retry-After` response header when the retry interval is known.

**Date and time conventions**
API audit timestamps (`date-time`) are returned in ISO 8601 UTC form with a `Z`
suffix. Persist and interpret audit timestamps in UTC, including setting the
MySQL session/application convention explicitly; MySQL `DATETIME` itself does
not store a timezone. Meeting and preferred times are campus-local calendar
dates and `HH:MM` times interpreted in one explicitly configured application
timezone. Do not rely on the server machine's implicit timezone. A combined
meeting date/time must be strictly later than the current time: today is
allowed only when the selected time has not passed. Apply this rule to both
meeting proposals and student reschedule requests.

**Route and contract decisions**
- US-12 and US-13 define submission behaviour but not route strings. This
  contract uses `POST /complaints/anonymous` and `POST /complaints/identified`.
- US-21's `PATCH /staff` wording does not identify the complaint being changed.
  This contract uses `PATCH /admin/complaints/{complaintId}/assignment`; the body
  accepts an active `staff_id` or `null` to unassign. `GET /admin/staff` lists
  active staff.
- US-22's `POST /notes` wording does not identify the parent complaint. This
  contract uses `POST /admin/complaints/{complaintId}/notes` so the note is
  unambiguously attached to the complaint.
- Status and meeting-proposal actions are similarly nested under
  `/admin/complaints/{complaintId}`. The admin meeting list is `GET /admin/meetings`.
- Student meeting actions are separate `POST /meetings/{meetingId}/confirm`
  and `POST /meetings/{meetingId}/reschedule` operations because they have
  different request and state-transition behaviour. Both require the tracking
  reference capability header, not an admin JWT.
- The admin complaint queue's reference search is case-insensitive. Normalize
  the supplied reference to uppercase before querying the case-sensitive
  `ascii_bin` tracking-reference column; use parameterized SQL.

This contract contains exactly 17 operations traced to US-04, US-07, US-09,
US-12, US-13, US-15, US-17, US-19, US-20, US-21, US-22, US-24, US-25, US-26,
and US-27. UI-only stories do not add API operations.

**Implementation dependencies that must not be overlooked**
- The `/health` operation is process liveness and must not depend on a live
  database query. The FastAPI app must not fail during import because a MySQL
  pool cannot connect; use safe/lazy initialization or otherwise allow the
  process to start and report liveness independently.
- Enforce the US-20 status-transition matrix in the service/database layer
  inside the same transaction that records status history. Documentation alone
  does not enforce the rule.
- Ensure meeting date/time comparisons use the configured campus timezone and
  that audit timestamps use UTC consistently.

servers.description: API v1 base path (local FastAPI default is http://localhost:8000/api/v1)

tags.name: Lookups
tags.description: Active values used to populate student forms.

tags.name: Student complaints
tags.description: Anonymous and identified complaint submission and tracking.

tags.name: Admin complaints
tags.description: Administrator complaint queue and complaint actions.

tags.name: Staff
tags.description: Active staff directory and complaint assignment.

tags.name: Meetings
tags.description: Administrator meeting management and student responses.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Administrator reporting based on the five database views.

get.description:
Returns process liveness only; this endpoint must not perform a database
query. Application startup must not fail solely because the database is
unavailable (for example, do not make a required MySQL connection at module
import time). Database readiness is a separate concern and is not represented
by this endpoint.

post.description:
Verifies the administrator email and password against the stored bcrypt
password hash. On success, updates `last_login_at` and returns a JWT that expires
after 8 hours. Wrong credentials return 401. An inactive administrator is not
allowed to access the admin area and receives 403. Under US-31, limit login to
5 attempts per 15-minute window; requests exceeding the limit return 429.

get.description:
Returns active complaint categories and their active options (including
the fixed option descriptions), active academic batches, and active
sections. Values are sourced from the lookup tables rather than hard-coded
into the API. This endpoint is public because students do not log in.

post.description:
Creates an anonymous complaint using a predefined option. The selected
option must belong to the selected category. Do not accept a student ID,
registration number, batch, section, class timing, or free-text description
on this operation. The server/database generates a unique `SVP-XXXXXX`
tracking reference and saves the initial `Received` history entry in the
same submission transaction.

Creates or updates the student record identified by registration number,
then creates an identified complaint. Registration number, batch, section,
class timing and a 20-1000 character description are required. Identified
submissions do not use a predefined anonymous option. The server generates
the tracking reference and returns it to the student.

example.description: The projector in Room 9 has not worked for a week and it affects lectures.

get.description:
Returns the complaint status, status history, latest resolution note and
current/latest meeting, if any. It must never return student identity fields
(including registration number, batch, section or class timing). For anonymous
complaints, it returns the predefined option, not free text. This is a public
capability endpoint: rate-limit requests and redact the reference from logs.

200.description: Complaint tracking information; no student identity is included.

get.summary: List complaints in the admin queue
get.description:
Returns 20 complaints per page, newest first. Supports category, status,
complaint type, date-range and tracking-reference search filters. Every
request requires an active administrator JWT.

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description: Include complaints submitted on or after this date.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: Include complaints submitted on or before this date; must not be earlier than date_from.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Case-insensitive partial search. The API normalizes the supplied value to uppercase before querying the case-sensitive tracking-reference column.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Page size is fixed at 20 by US-17.

get.description:
Returns the full administrative details, including status history, notes,
assignment and meeting information. For anonymous complaints, student
identity properties are omitted entirely. For identified complaints,
the response may include registration number, batch, section and class
timing. Requires an active administrator JWT.

200.description: Complaint detail. The response shape depends on complaint mode.

patch.description:
Changes status and writes a status-history row in the same transaction.
Allowed transitions are: Received -> Under Review or Rejected;
Under Review -> Resolved or Rejected; Resolved -> Under Review; and
Rejected -> Under Review. Unchanged or disallowed transitions return 422.
Requires an active administrator JWT.

Assigns an active staff member to this complaint. Set `staff_id` to
`null` to make the complaint Unassigned. This is the complaint-scoped route
chosen to clarify the backlog's underspecified `PATCH /staff` requirement.
Requires an active administrator JWT.

get.description: Returns active staff members for complaint assignment. Requires an active administrator JWT.

post.description:
Saves a 10-500 character resolution/response note with the authenticated
administrator as its author and a creation timestamp. The newest note is
exposed on the student's tracking response. Requires an active admin JWT.

example.note_text: The projector has been inspected and a replacement has been scheduled.

post.summary: Propose a meeting for an identified complaint
post.description:
Creates a meeting proposal for an identified complaint only. Anonymous
complaints are rejected with 422. The meeting date cannot be in the past, and
the combined local date/time must be strictly later than the current time. A
same-day meeting is allowed only when its time has not passed. The location
must be 3-100 characters and the optional message is limited to 300 characters.
A new proposal starts with `No Response`. Requires an active administrator JWT.

Allows the student associated with the meeting's complaint to confirm it.
The student has no account; the server must validate the supplied tracking
reference against the meeting's complaint. If a reschedule request exists,
it is removed before the meeting is marked Confirmed. Repeating confirmation
for an already-confirmed meeting returns 409.

Allows the student associated with the meeting's complaint to request a
different date and time. The tracking reference must match the complaint
associated with the meeting. The combined preferred local date/time must be
strictly later than the current time; today is allowed only when the selected
time has not passed. The optional message is limited to 300 characters. A
meeting can have at most one outstanding reschedule request. Requests after
the meeting has already been answered return 409.

example.message: I have a lab session at the proposed time.

201.description: Reschedule request created and meeting response set to Requested Different Time.

get.description:
Returns meeting proposals for administrator monitoring. Supports filtering
by student response (`No Response`, `Confirmed`, or `Requested Different Time`).
Each item can include the student's requested alternate date/time. Requires
an active administrator JWT.

parameters.name: response
parameters.description: Filter by the student's response to the proposed meeting.

get.description:
Returns overall totals and the data represented by the five SQL views:
status summary, resolution rate, category summary, monthly volume and
class-timing summary. Staff workload is also included as a grouped count
by assigned staff member. Requires an active administrator JWT.

bearerAuth.description: Administrator JWT. Issued by POST /auth/login and valid for 8 hours.

trackingReference.name: X-Tracking-Reference
trackingReference.description:
Student tracking reference carried in `X-Tracking-Reference` for meeting
responses. The server must verify that it belongs to the complaint associated
with the meeting. This is a capability secret: rate-limit its use and never log
its raw value. Students do not have accounts in this project.

TrackingReferencePath.name: ref
TrackingReferencePath.description:
Generated tracking reference; format `SVP-` followed by six uppercase letters
or digits. Treat it as a capability secret. The format provides approximately
31 bits of entropy, so enforce rate limiting and do not expose the reference in
application logs, access logs, analytics, or error messages.

code.description: Stable application error code (for example NOT_FOUND or VALIDATION_ERROR).

message.description: Human-readable summary. Must not expose stack traces or secrets.

fields.description:
Field-level errors. Use an empty object when no field-specific
details exist. A value is one message or a list of messages when
multiple validation rules fail for the same field.

access_token.description: Signed JWT. Treat as a secret.

AnonymousComplaintRequest.description: No identity fields or free-text description are accepted for anonymous submissions.

batch_id.description: Must identify an active academic batch returned by GET /lookups.

section_id.description: Must identify an active section returned by GET /lookups.

description.description: Trimmed free-text complaint description; whitespace-only values are invalid.

old_status.description: Null for the initial Received history row.

TrackingResponse.description: Deliberately excludes all student identity fields for both complaint modes.

option.description: Present for anonymous complaints; null for identified complaints.

description.description: Present for identified complaints; null for anonymous complaints.

meeting.description: Current/latest meeting for an identified complaint, or null if none exists.

old_status.description: Null for the initial Received history row.

AdminAnonymousComplaintDetail.description: Anonymous response intentionally excludes description and all student identity properties.

staff_id.description: Active staff ID, or null to unassign the complaint.

note_text.description: Trimmed note text; whitespace-only values are invalid.

meeting_date.description: Campus-local date. Cannot be before today; when the date is today, meeting_time must still be in the future.

meeting_time.description: Campus-local time in HH:MM format. Combined with meeting_date, it must be strictly later than current time.

preferred_date.description: Campus-local date. Combined with preferred_time, it must be strictly later than current time; today is allowed only if the time has not passed.

preferred_time.description: Campus-local time in HH:MM format. Combined with preferred_date, it must be strictly later than current time.

resolved.description: May be null when the database contains no complaints.

resolution_rate_percent.description: Null when there are no complaints.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired credentials (or invalid tracking reference for a meeting response).

Forbidden.description: Authenticated administrator is inactive or not permitted to perform the operation.

NotFound.description: The requested resource or tracking reference does not exist.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The HTTP method is not supported for this path.

Conflict.description: Operation conflicts with the resource's current state (for example, a meeting has already been answered).

error.message: The operation conflicts with the current resource state

ValidationError.description: Request validation or a business-rule validation failed.

description: Description must contain at least 20 characters.

fields.request: Request body is not valid JSON

InternalServerError.description: Unexpected server error. Internal exception details are logged server-side and are not returned to the client.

error.message: Something went wrong on the server

DefaultError.description: Any other HTTP error. The same standard error envelope is returned.

TooManyRequests.description: The caller exceeded the configured rate limit. Retry after the indicated interval when supplied.

Retry-After.description: Number of seconds the client should wait before retrying, when known.
